title: Forward Pass
subtext: How a neural network makes a prediction
author: Buzzpy

description.title: Forward Pass
texts: A forward pass is the process of feeding input data through a neural network, layer by layer, to produce an output (prediction). Each layer transforms the data using weights and activation functions until a final result is reached.

During training, the forward pass runs first to generate a prediction. That prediction is then compared against the correct answer to calculate how wrong the model was — this error is called the loss.
The term 'forward' refers to the direction of data flow: input → hidden layers → output. No weights are updated during this step; it is purely a computation pass.
